snip.t: Complications arise when exudate becomes loculated → Parapneumonic effusion / empyema, or when necrosis → Lung abscess, especially with *Staph aureus* or *Klebsiella*.

Parapneumonic effusion and empyema, lung abscess, sepsis and septic shock, respiratory failure and ARDS, pleurisy, pericarditis, lobar collapse, metastatic infection (meningitis, endocarditis, arthritis), bronchiectasis (long term).
Recurrent infection, massive haemoptysis, empyema, lung abscess, pneumothorax, respiratory failure and cor pulmonale, amyloidosis, metastatic infection (brain abscess), sinusitis.
Mucociliary clearance: Dysfunction (alcohol, smoking, neuromuscular disease) diminishes removal of secretions, allowing bacterial colonisation and progression to abscess formation.
Drainage: ultrasound-guided percutaneous drainage, or drainage through the vagina (colpotomy) for a pouch of Douglas abscess.
Surgery: laparoscopy or laparotomy for rupture, failure of antibiotics after 48 to 72 hours, or a large abscess.

qs.q: A 42-year-old immigrant from an endemic region presents with a single right hepatic lobe abscess. Serological testing for anti-amoebic antibodies is ordered. Which of the following best describes the clinical interpretation of this test?
o: A positive test distinguishes active from past infection
A negative test assists in excluding the diagnosis
A negative titer mandates repeat testing in one week
A positive titer correlates directly with abscess size
qs.e: Due to high baseline exposure in endemic zones, serological testing has a high negative predictive value, meaning a negative test assists in excluding the infection. Conversely, positive titers persist for years and cannot confirm acute disease.

qs.q: When is therapeutic needle aspiration specifically indicated in the management of a suspected amoebic liver abscess?
o: To differentiate amoebic from pyogenic pus
When no response to therapy occurs in days
To prevent the development of effusion
As a routine first-line diagnostic procedure
qs.e: Aspiration is not conventionally required unless there is no response to therapy after 3-5 days or the abscess is at immediate risk of rupture. Routine aspiration is discouraged because medical therapy is highly effective.

qs.q: What is the characteristic macroscopic appearance of the fluid obtained from an aspirated amoebic liver abscess?
qs.e: The aspirate consists of an acellular proteinaceous debris described as chocolate-colored anchovy paste fluid. Purulent green pus is more typical of pyogenic bacterial abscesses.

qs.q: A 35-year-old male with a severe skin abscess requires an oral antibiotic with 100% bioavailability, excellent intracellular penetration, and a high volume of distribution. Which of the following is the best choice?
qs.e: Fluoroquinolones possess high oral bioavailability and a high volume of distribution enabling excellent tissue and intracellular penetration. In contrast, aminoglycosides and vancomycin have low volumes of distribution and poor oral absorption.

qs.q: A patient presents with a brain abscess containing darkly pigmented septate hyphae. Which organism is most likely responsible?
qs.e: Phaeohyphomycosis, which can present as a brain abscess with pigmented hyphae, is caused by Cladophialophora species. Madurella causes mycetoma, and Sporothrix causes lymphangitic spread.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Fundamentals: Fungi, Antifungal Drugs & More: MCQs

qs.q: A patient presents with a brain abscess, and pathology reveals darkly pigmented septate hyphae. Which genus is the most likely causative agent?
qs.e: Phaeohyphomycosis presenting as a brain abscess with darkly pigmented septate hyphae is typically caused by Cladophialophora species. Histoplasma capsulatum typically presents as yeast within macrophages rather than pigmented hyphae.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Fundamentals: Fungi, Antifungal Drugs & More: MCQs

qs.q: What is the recommended first-line imaging modality for screening when acute lobar nephronia or renal abscess is suspected?
qs.e: Ultrasound is the first-line type of imaging for screening and will likely demonstrate an enlarged kidney with a possible mass. A CT scan is more sensitive and specific, typically showing a wedge-shaped lower-density area.

qs.q: A patient presents with a suspected amoebic liver abscess. Which of the following laboratory findings is typically present in the peripheral blood?
qs.e: Peripheral blood testing in hepatic amoebiasis typically demonstrates leucocytosis without eosinophilia. Eosinophilia is characteristic of helminthic infections rather than amoebic liver abscesses.
